chunks: Ibn Nuh said: I have prepared this copy from two ancient scrolls, which contained letters and epistles.
ai.seo_question: What was the source material for Ibn Nuh's copy of the hadith?
ai.summary: Ibn Nuh clarifies that his manuscript was transcribed from two ancient scrolls (al-Mudrajayn) which featured both the text and the Prophet’s or Imams’ signatures, a detail crucial for establishing the chain of transmission (isnad) in Shia hadith scholarship. This reference highlights the meticulous preservation methods used by early scholars to authenticate the authenticity of the Imam's words through physical evidence of their handwriting and seals.
